description: Frontend developer (Next.js, React, TypeScript) with UI design skills, joining NASA Space Apps with an experienced backend developer. We’re looking for a data analyst or ML enthusiast who can work with NASA datasets, plus someone interested in storytelling and presentation. Open to all levels. Let’s build something great together!
summary: SkyBlink turns raw SPHEREx infrared sky data into a telescope-style web tool that anyone can use. SPHEREx maps the whole sky every six months, and moving objects such as comets shift between its images, but the data comes as large FITS files that only specialists can open. SkyBlink lets users pick a featured target or sky region, drag a time slider, play the frames as an animation, or blink between two dates so the stars stay fixed and moving objects jump out. Frames come from real SPHEREx images, prepared with a Python pipeline (astropy, reproject), aligned to a common sky grid, and served by a Node.js backend to a Next.js interface. Every frame shows its date and wavelength, and any estimated motion is clearly labeled. Our goal is to make NASA's infrared sky survey understandable to students, teachers and curious people, with no astronomy or coding skills needed.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

SkyBlink is a public web app shaped like a telescope eyepiece. Users choose a featured target (for example the interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS) or a sky region, then explore real SPHEREx images over time with a time slider, a play/pause animation, and a Blink mode that flips between two dates. Background stars stay fixed while moving objects shift, so change is visible at a glance. Each frame shows its date and wavelength.

HOW IT WORKS

1. A Python pipeline queries the NASA/IPAC IRSA SPHEREx archive (SIA2) and requests small cutouts around each target.

2. Cutouts are aligned to a common sky grid (astropy WCS + reproject), normalized with one brightness scale per target, and exported as lightweight WebP frames with a JSON manifest.

3. A Node.js backend serves the manifest and frames, and a Next.js frontend renders the viewer. Frames are prepared ahead of time, so the site is fast and does not depend on a live archive connection.

WHY IT MATTERS

SPHEREx maps the whole sky every six months, but its data lives in large scientific files. SkyBlink gives students, teachers and curious people a simple way to see the sky change, with no astronomy or coding background. It also teaches how astronomers find moving objects: the blink comparator method historically used to discover Pluto.

CREATIVITY

The whole interface is built around the blink comparator idea: a circular eyepiece, a plate-strip timeline, and a one-button Blink that makes motion obvious in seconds.

SCIENTIFIC HONESTY

- SPHEREx images are taken at different wavelengths across the detector, so brightness differences between frames can come from wavelength, not real change. We focus on position changes and show every frame's wavelength.

TOOLS

Python (astropy, reproject, numpy, Pillow), Node.js, React.js, TypeScript, deployed on Vercel .

CODE: https://github.com/Mohamed-Mos-aad/SkyBlink

USE OF SUPER INTELLIGENCE (SI)

We used AI assistants during planning and development: Claude (Anthropic) for brainstorming, documentation and drafting text and code, and Google Stitch for UI mockups. [Parts of the code were AI-assisted and are marked in the README and file headers.] [SI-generated mockup images carry a visible "SI-generated" watermark.] No NASA logos or branding were generated or used.

Data credit: NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive (SPHEREx). SkyBlink is a hackathon project for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 and is not an official NASA product.
